policy_title: Enact Socio-economic Duty and Introduce Race Equality Act
stated: Labour will enact the socio-economic duty in the Equality Act 2010. They will introduce a landmark Race Equality Act to enshrine equal pay rights for Black, Asian, and other ethnic minority people, strengthen protections against dual discrimination, and address other racial inequalities. The party will reverse the Conservatives’ decision to downgrade monitoring of antisemitic and Islamophobic hate, and introduce ethnicity pay gap reporting for large employers.

source.quote: Labour will ensure no matter whatever your background, you can thrive, and therefore we will enact the socio-economic duty in the Equality Act 2010. Labour will introduce a landmark Race Equality Act, to enshrine in law the full right to equal pay for Black, Asian, and other ethnic minority people, strengthen protections against dual discrimination and root out other racial inequalities. Labour will also reverse the Conservatives’ decision to downgrade the monitoring of antisemitic and Islamophobic hate. Building on gender pay gap reporting, we will introduce disability and ethnicity pay gap reporting for large employers.

bearing_set.reason: The Race Equality Act enshrines anti-discrimination protections and equal treatment rights for ethnic minorities; the socio-economic duty extends legal protection against disadvantage; dual-discrimination strengthening and hate-monitoring reversal are squarely within civil rights and equal-treatment scope.

Equal pay rights for Black, Asian, and ethnic minority workers and mandatory ethnicity pay gap reporting for large employers directly affect pay levels and fairness in employment for a substantial share of the workforce.

Reversing the downgrading of antisemitic and Islamophobic hate-crime monitoring restores the data infrastructure for charge and conviction tracking of hate crimes, concretely affecting O5's crime-rate and charge/conviction indicators for targeted communities.

The socio-economic duty compels public bodies to actively reduce inequality of outcome from socioeconomic disadvantage; ethnicity pay gap reporting and equal pay rights mechanically narrow the income gap between ethnic minority workers and others — both directly move inequality indicators.

Reversing the downgrading of antisemitic and Islamophobic hate monitoring directly affects hate-crime tracking (an explicit O15 indicator), and the Race Equality Act addressing racial inequalities bears on inter-group relations and integration.

membership_note: Four genuine bearings: the policy is primarily an equal-treatment measure (O9) with real distributional labour-market effects (O4, O14) and a specific community cohesion component via hate monitoring (O15). No material bearing on public finances (O12) or liberty (O10) — employer reporting obligations are too minor to clear the non-negligible bar on O10.
